headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Replit Agent can read/write persistent Repl files while agentic-flow can modify git and use MCP, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b can read and write Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if either agent consumes the other's file output as trusted input. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high, but the shared workspace path is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF agent_a writes prompts or tool output into files that agent_b later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF agent_b ingests workspace files without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer its actions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Add a provenance header check before agent_b reads any file from agent_a.
Disable MCP routes that accept free-form text from shared files.
Use a human review step for any cross-agent handoff file.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts, and agent_b touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Because agent_b has persistent Repl filesystem access and agent_a can interact with GitHub/MCP, a shared-workspace or handoff leak is plausible. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, sensitive code or secrets can flow from agent_b to agent_a outputs.
IF agent_a forwards file contents through MCP or GitHub APIs, data touched by agent_b can leave the Repl boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared repo files.
Store credentials only in the platform secret store.
Restrict agent_a to non-sensitive branches or mirrors.
Review any file export before it leaves the Repl.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and modify git state. agent_b also has write_filesystem and persistent Repl filesystem state, while agent_a can use MCP and background workers. Concurrent writes to the same repo or git state without locking can corrupt work or overwrite changes, matching the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git branch or working tree, concurrent commits or file writes can race.
IF either agent runs package installs during the other's edits, dependency drift or lockfile churn can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent package installs.
Use a merge gate before pushing changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs through MCP and GitHub-facing workflows, and agent_b can act inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. The profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream actions, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated plans without verification, incorrect facts can be operationalized.
IF agent_a emits malformed code or commands and agent_b executes them, the error propagates downstream.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Ask agent_a to include source links or diffs for claims.
Limit agent_b to draft-only mode for cross-agent tasks.
Add a human approval checkpoint for deployments.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a Replit-managed cloud Repl, while agent_a handles Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not establish a residency mismatch or specific regulatory boundary, but they do show different data classes and retention surfaces, so a compliance-policy mismatch is plausible and medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the Repl workspace, platform retention and residency rules may apply.
IF secrets are copied into files instead of the secret store, compliance controls can be bypassed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use the secret store instead of plaintext files.
Document the data residency of each workspace.
Delete temporary exports after review.
